summary: Defines a new IANA registry for the values of the SIP Priority header field and updates RFC 3261 accordingly. This gives a central place to record those values.

eli5.summary: A shared notebook where everyone writes down the official priority words a phone call can have.

questions: is there an iana registry for sip priority
what values can the sip priority header have
what is the policy for new sip priority values
subtitle: Creates an IANA registry for the values of the SIP Priority header field.

tldr.problem: The SIP Priority header field was designed to allow new values, but no registry had ever been set up to record them.
tldr.mechanism: A new sub-registry, Priority Header Field Values, is added with the four values from RFC 3261 and the IETF Review policy.
tldr.outcome: New Priority values now need IETF Review because of their potential architectural impact.

today: RFC 6878 is a Proposed Standard from March 2013 that updates RFC 3261. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: The SIP Priority header field was defined in Section 20.26 of RFC 3261. It was specified so that new values could be created, but no registry had been established. This document defines one.
sections.eli5: People could invent new priority words, but nobody kept a list. Now there is one.

sections.title: The New Registry
sections.content:
The sub-registry "Priority Header Field Values" is added to the "Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) Parameters" page. Its initial values, all referencing RFC 3261, are non-urgent, normal, urgent and emergency.

The registration policy is "IETF Review" from RFC 5226, chosen over lighter policies because new values could affect the architecture. Anyone considering a new value should ask whether SIP Resource-Priority (RFC 4412) or a different protocol would fit better.
sections.eli5: The list starts with four words. To add a fifth, a group of experts must agree, and you should check whether another tool already does the job.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document has no impact on the security of SIP. Its purpose is purely administrative in nature: it records existing values and sets a registration policy.
sections.eli5: It only starts a list, so it changes nothing about safety.

references.text: Rosenberg, J., et al., "SIP: Session Initiation Protocol", RFC 3261, June 2002.
Narten, T. and H. Alvestrand, "Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs", BCP 26, RFC 5226, May 2008.
Schulzrinne, H. and J. Polk, "Communications Resource Priority for the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP)", RFC 4412, February 2006.
